n: Judah’s sin is engraved with an iron tool and a diamond point on the tablets of their hearts and on the horns of their altars. God once wrote His law on stone; now sin is etched deep inside them.

f.w: a pen of iron
f.g: An iron stylus for carving stone.

f.w: the table of their heart
the horns of your altars
f.g: The raised corners of an altar, where sacrificial blood was smeared for atonement (Leviticus 4:7).

n: Their children remember their pagan altars and Asherah poles by every green tree on the high hills. Idolatry has been passed to the next generation.

f.w: groves
f.g: Asherah poles—wooden symbols of the goddess Asherah.

n: God’s mountain (Jerusalem) and all its treasures will be plundered because of sin at its high places throughout the land.

f.w: O my mountain in the field

n: Through your own fault you’ll lose the inheritance God gave you, and serve enemies in a strange land. You’ve lit a fire in God’s anger that will burn on.

f.w: discontinue from thine heritage
f.g: Let go of—lose—your inheritance, as in the sabbatical year when land was released.

f.w: which shall burn for ever

n: A famous contrast in wisdom style: cursed is the person who trusts in mere humans, relies on human strength, and turns his heart from the Lord. Nephi echoes this almost exactly.

f.w: Cursed be the man that trusteth in man
maketh flesh his arm
f.g: Relies on human power for strength.

n: Such a person is like a scrubby bush in the desert that never sees good come—living in parched, salty, empty land.

f.w: the heath in the desert
f.g: A stunted desert shrub, perhaps the juniper.

f.w: a salt land
f.g: Barren salt flats where nothing grows, like near the Dead Sea.

n: But blessed is the person who trusts in the Lord, whose confidence is the Lord Himself.

f.w: Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD

n: He is like a tree planted by water, sending roots down to the stream. It doesn’t fear the heat; its leaves stay green and it keeps bearing fruit even in drought. Trust in God gives deep roots that hold in hard seasons.

f.w: as a tree planted by the waters
shall not be careful in the year of drought

n: The heart is more deceitful than anything and desperately sick—who can understand it? We can fool even ourselves, which is why we need God’s searching light.

f.w: The heart is deceitful above all things
desperately wicked

n: God answers: I, the Lord, search the heart and test the inner self, to give each person what his actions and choices deserve.

f.w: I the LORD search the heart
according to the fruit of his doings

n: Like a partridge sitting on eggs she didn’t lay (an ancient belief), a person who gets rich dishonestly will lose it in midlife and end up a fool.

f.w: As the partridge sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not
f.g: Ancient folk belief held that the partridge hatched other birds’ eggs, whose chicks then left her.

f.w: he that getteth riches, and not by right

n: Jeremiah praises: a glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary—God’s presence in the temple.

f.w: A glorious high throne

n: O Lord, Hope of Israel, all who abandon You will be ashamed; those who turn away will be written in the dust—quickly erased—because they forsook the Lord, the fountain of living water. Some connect this with Jesus writing in the dust in John 8.

f.w: the fountain of living waters
written in the earth
f.g: Names written in dust, soon blotted out—unlike names written in the book of life.

n: Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for You are the one I praise. True healing and salvation come only from God.

f.w: Heal me, O LORD, and I shall be healed

n: People taunt Jeremiah: “Where is this word of the Lord you keep predicting? Let it happen!” Mockers often scoff when judgment seems delayed.

f.w: Where is the word of the LORD?

n: Jeremiah protests his sincerity: I didn’t run from being Your shepherd, and I never wanted the day of disaster. You know what I said was right before You.

f.w: neither have I desired the woeful day

n: Don’t become a terror to me; You are my refuge in the day of disaster.

f.w: thou art my hope in the day of evil

n: Let my persecutors be shamed, not me; let them be terrified, not me. Bring on them the day of disaster with double destruction. Honest prayers in scripture sometimes voice raw feelings that the gospel of Christ later invites us to transform into forgiveness.

f.w: Let them be confounded that persecute me

n: God sends Jeremiah to stand at the People’s Gate, used by the kings, and at all of Jerusalem’s gates—the busiest public places.

f.w: the gate of the children of the people
f.g: Probably a main city gate used by the public and the royal household.

n: Listen, kings of Judah and all who come through these gates.
Be careful: don’t carry loads or bring goods through Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath. Commerce on the Sabbath had become normal.

f.w: bear no burden on the sabbath day

n: Don’t carry loads out of your houses or do any work, but keep the Sabbath holy as God commanded your ancestors.

f.w: hallow ye the sabbath day
hallow

n: But their ancestors didn’t listen—they stiffened their necks and refused to be taught.

f.w: made their neck stiff

n: If you carefully obey and keep the Sabbath holy, doing no work on it...

f.w: if ye diligently hearken unto me

n: …then kings on David’s throne will keep riding through these gates with their officials and people, and this city will be inhabited forever. Small acts of obedience carry big blessings.

f.w: sitting upon the throne of David

n: People will come from all over—Judah’s towns, Benjamin, the western foothills, the hill country, and the Negev—bringing offerings, incense, and thanksgiving to the Lord’s house.

f.w: the plain
f.g: The Shephelah—the low foothills west of Judah.

f.w: the south
sacrifices of praise

n: But if you won’t keep the Sabbath holy and keep hauling loads through the gates, God will set fire to the gates that will consume Jerusalem’s palaces and can’t be put out. Babylon burned the city in 586 BC.

f.w: then will I kindle a fire in the gates thereof
